title: Hiring a bike — impact of the pricing change
subtitle: Fictional demo data — an invented bike hire operator. Not from any real organisation.

steps.name: Find a bike
action: Open the app and look at the map
Walk to the nearest available bike
insight: Availability shown in the app doesn't always match what's on the street.
Wants to know the cost before committing to the walk.

changes.quote: the applicable rate must be shown on the bike detail screen

steps.reason: The rider checks the map here, so the rate may need to appear earlier than the bike detail screen.

steps.name: Unlock
action: Scan the code on the bike
Wait for the lock to release
insight: Confirming a price without knowing how long the ride will take feels uncertain.
No way to check the off-peak cut-off before starting.

changes.quote: riders are charged per minute of active hire, with a daily cap
rides starting between 10:00 and 15:00 are charged at 60%
shown on the bike detail screen before the rider unlocks

steps.reason: The unlock is where the rate is now fixed, so the rate and its band have to be visible and correct here.

steps.name: Ride
insight: Stopping now costs money, which changes how the rider behaves.
No sense of what the ride has cost so far.

changes.quote: the app shows a running total, updated at least every 60 seconds

steps.reason: Nothing is shown during a ride today, so the running total is a new element in this step.

steps.name: Report a fault
action: Report the fault in the app
Wait to hear whether the ride is still being charged
insight: Doesn't know whether the meter is still running while the fault is reviewed.
Expects the charge to stop the moment the fault is reported, not when it's confirmed.

changes.quote: time is not charged when a ride is interrupted by a mechanical fault, once confirmed
advisors need a tool that reconstructs how a fare was calculated

steps.reason: The policy says charging stops once confirmed, but not what happens between reporting and confirmation.

steps.name: End the hire
insight: The final figure is the first hard number the rider has seen.
Wants to understand which rate applied before deciding whether to query it.

changes.quote: receipts must show duration, rate band applied, and any cap reached

steps.reason: The fare is finalised here, and the receipt content is explicitly changed by CH-05.

steps.name: Query a charge
action: Explain when and where the ride happened
insight: Has to describe the ride from memory because the receipt doesn't explain the calculation.
No visibility of how long a decision will take.

changes.quote: a tool that reconstructs how a fare was calculated, to answer disputes

steps.reason: Advisors cannot answer per-minute disputes with today's account screen, so a lookup step has to exist.
